note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: The observational analogue of an intention-to-treat effect contrasts assigning initiation now against not initiating now. Two things then happen that do not happen in a randomized trial. Assignment is confounded, so the contrast requires baseline adjustment to mean anything. And the comparator group does not stay untreated: patients assigned to no initiation now frequently initiate later, so with longer follow-up the two strategies converge and the estimated effect attenuates toward the null for reasons that have nothing to do with the treatment's efficacy. The attenuation is a function of the follow-up horizon and of local prescribing behavior, and it is rarely reported as such, so an emulation with long follow-up and a null result cannot be distinguished from one where the treatment does not work.
problems.correction_note: Two errors. Crossover into the comparator arm happens in randomized trials as well, so it is not something that happens only in an emulation. And attenuation toward the null is not guaranteed: the direction and size depend on the treatment-effect dynamics, the switching mechanism, competing events and the effect scale, so a convergence rate alone does not determine an attenuation factor. Methods for handling treatment switching also exist and have been reviewed, which the entry did not acknowledge.
problems.statement: The observational analogue of an intention-to-treat effect contrasts assigning initiation now against not initiating now, and in that contrast the comparator group does not stay untreated: patients frequently initiate later. Reduced separation between the treatment histories can move the estimated effect at longer horizons, in a direction and by an amount that depend on the treatment-effect dynamics, the switching mechanism, the competing events and the effect scale. This is a feature of the estimand rather than a bias to be removed, and it occurs in randomized trials too. What emulations do not do is report it: the cumulative incidence of initiation in each arm over follow-up is rarely published, so a reader cannot judge how far the contrasted strategies stayed distinct, and a null result at a long horizon cannot be read against the convergence that actually occurred.
problems.why_open: The convergence is a property of the strategy contrast, so it cannot be adjusted away without changing to a per-protocol estimand that carries its own assumptions, and methods for that exist. The reporting gap is what remains, and it persists because the trajectories are an extra analysis that weakens no result and strengthens none. There is also no convention for choosing the horizon at which an open-ended no-initiation arm is still a meaningful comparator, and the rate of convergence depends on the health system and calendar period rather than on anything intrinsic to the treatment.
problems.proposed_direction: Report the cumulative incidence of initiation in both arms over follow-up alongside the effect estimate, so the separation between strategies is visible rather than assumed. Prefer contrasts that name the later initiation explicitly, such as initiate now versus initiate on a stated clinical trigger, over an open-ended no-initiation arm the data will not sustain, and use the existing switching methods when the per-protocol question is the one being asked. Quantify by simulation how a given convergence rate moves the estimate at each horizon under different effect dynamics, so the reader has something to read a null against.

prior_work.cite: Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
prior_work.what_it_does: Defines the observational analogues of the intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects and states what each requires.

prior_work.cite: Cain LE, Robins JM, Lanoy E, Logan R, Costagliola D, Hernán MA. Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies. Int J Epidemiol 2016;45(6):2038-2049
prior_work.what_it_does: Handles later initiation and switching explicitly through dynamic strategies, which is the design response to convergence.

prior_work.cite: Statistical methods to adjust for treatment switching in real-world clinical studies: a scoping review and decision framework. Clin Pharmacol Ther 2025
prior_work.what_it_does: Catalogs the available methods for treatment switching and supplies a framework for choosing among them, which is the body of work the entry originally overlooked.

prior_work.cite: Caution in handling switchers in pharmacoepidemiologic studies estimating treatment effects. Am J Epidemiol 2026
prior_work.what_it_does: Sets out the analytic hazards specific to switchers in effect estimation.
